messages:
Dev Patel: pulling together support readiness for Usage Insights beta/GA. Expecting a bunch of tickets around (1) invoice vs console mismatch, (2) “Unknown route” dominating top drivers, (3) export CSV limitations/timeouts. Can we align on canned responses + a known issues list we can paste into Zendesk macros?

Paula Mendes: yep. we should have a short “why totals differ” explanation + what to check first. Nadia can you sanity check the technical bits?

Nadia Rahman: +1. biggest reasons we’ve seen in dogfood:
- timing: console insights are near-real-time but metering can arrive late / be corrected; invoice is authoritative + finalized
- filtering: console route views respect project/env/region/deployment mode filters; invoices are usually org-level (or include multiple projects)
- cached tokens: insights shows cached tokens separately; some folks assume cache is “free” and get confused
- missing route tag -> everything shows as `unknown` (sdk not updated or header stripped at gateway)

Dev Patel: perfect. can you give me wording that won’t get us in trouble (i.e., not saying invoice is wrong) and a checklist for triage?

Rishi Malhotra: from Finance perspective: keep it crisp: “invoice is source of truth; insights are diagnostic + may differ due to timing + scope.” also mention that discounts/credits/taxes won’t show in route insights. folks will try to reconcile to the penny.

Elliot Price: docs-wise we can add an FAQ section and link support to it. draft answer:
“Usage Insights attributes compute/token usage to routes and models to help you understand drivers. Invoice totals may differ because invoices are finalized after late-arriving usage is processed and may include adjustments (credits/discounts), while console dashboards show operational telemetry within your selected filters/time window.”

Allison Grant: also mention data freshness explicitly. we’re seeing ~2–5 min typical, but spikes up to ~20–30 min during backfill/recompute or pipeline lag. support should ask for:
- time range
- region
- whether they’re looking at hour vs day rollups
- and if there was an incident / lag spike

Kevin Osei: for exports: highlight the audit logging behavior. every export job creation + download emits audit events with requester, org/project, time window, and filters. customers will ask “is this logged?”

Dev Patel: ok. here’s a proposed macro draft #1 (invoice mismatch). edits welcome:

---
Macro: “Invoice totals vs Usage Insights totals”
Thanks for the report. Invoices are the source of truth for billed usage.
Usage Insights is a near-real-time, filtered diagnostic view to help attribute cost/latency by route and model. It can differ from invoice totals for a few common reasons:
1) Timing/freshness: some usage can arrive late or be corrected after initial processing.
2) Scope/filters: the console view reflects your selected org/project/environment/region/deployment mode and time window; invoices may aggregate across multiple projects and include other adjustments.
3) Adjustments: credits/discounts/taxes and other billing adjustments are reflected on invoices but not attributed to routes/models.

To help us investigate, please share:
- the exact time range and filters used in the console
- the invoice period you’re comparing against
- the export (CSV/JSON) if possible
---

Nadia Rahman: looks good. one nuance: “corrected after initial processing” — fine, but avoid sounding like we change numbers arbitrarily. maybe: “some usage events are processed with delay; totals can update as late data is ingested.”

Paula Mendes: +1. Also add “Usage Insights is not intended for billing reconciliation.” (gently)

Dev Patel: updated:
“Usage Insights isn’t intended for billing reconciliation; it’s designed to identify cost drivers and performance by route/model.”

Monica Patel: for “Unknown route” tickets, we should point to SDK route tagging guidance and note that older SDK versions won’t send the `route` field/header. also: if they’re using a custom gateway, it might strip headers. common gotcha.

Dev Patel: macro draft #2 (Unknown route):

---
Macro: “Unknown route in Usage Insights”
If “Unknown route” is a top cost driver, it usually means requests are missing a route identifier.
Common causes:
- SDK/client not setting `route` (or using an older SDK version that doesn’t support route tagging)
- a gateway/proxy stripping the route header
- dynamic/invalid route values being normalized/rolled up

Next steps:
1) Confirm your SDK version and set a stable route name (ex: `chat.generate`, `search.rerank`) for each endpoint.
2) If using a gateway, ensure the route header is forwarded.
3) After updating, new requests will show the route; historical data may remain “Unknown” depending on retention/backfill.
---

Elliot Price: “dynamic/invalid route values being normalized/rolled up” might be confusing. maybe say: “If route names are too long or high-cardinality, they may be truncated or aggregated.” and link to naming conventions.

Allison Grant: + mention there’s a propagation delay; don’t expect it to flip instantly. “allow a few minutes” is enough.

Kevin Osei: also: when route is missing, export still works but will have `route=unknown`. customers sometimes think export “lost” data.

Dev Patel: macro draft #3 (export timeouts / limits):

---
Macro: “Usage Insights export limits / timeouts”
Exports are designed for bounded time windows and may fail for large ranges.
Try:
- reduce the time range (ex: export one day at a time)
- filter by project/environment/region to reduce rows
- prefer JSON export for automation (stable schema) and CSV for ad-hoc analysis
If you still see failures, share the export job ID and approximate time window/filters.
---

Paula Mendes: add a line that scheduled exports aren’t supported yet (people will ask). but phrase as “not currently available” + suggest workaround.

Rishi Malhotra: workaround suggestion: “manual weekly export + upload to your internal system” or “use API to pull aggregated endpoints” (if we have it). but don’t promise a cron feature.

Nadia Rahman: we do have export job API (behind feature flag in beta). could suggest “use export API to trigger on your side” if enabled. but support should check if customer has access.

Dev Patel: got it. adding:
“Scheduled/recurring exports aren’t currently supported in the console. Some customers automate via the Export Jobs API (if enabled for your org) to generate and download reports on a schedule.”

Kevin Osei: make sure support mentions RBAC: exports only include data the requester can access; if they’re missing rows it may be permissions.

Dev Patel: good call. adding a bullet: “RBAC: exports respect org/project access; ensure the requester has access to the projects included in filters.”

Elliot Price: can we keep a “Known issues (beta)” list in one place? I can add a docs page section + we can mirror in an internal support doc. Proposed list:
- invoice vs console mismatch (timing/scope/adjustments)
- `Unknown route` due to missing tagging
- route normalization/truncation for overly long names
- hourly rollups can lag more than daily during high load
- export jobs fail for large time windows (limits)
- model fallback attribution: spend is tied to the original route; model breakdown reflects the actual model used, but during fallbacks you may see multiple models under one route

Allison Grant: add: “During incidents / degraded telemetry pipeline, dashboards may show partial data; check status page / pipeline lag metric.”

Paula Mendes: + a “Available starting” note: route/model breakdown only for data after enablement date (no backfill initially). otherwise people will complain last month is blank.

Dev Patel: awesome. I’ll turn this into:
1) 3 zendesk macros
2) internal “Usage Insights Known Issues” page
3) a quick support triage checklist (ask filters/time range/export job ID)

If anyone has strong opinions on language, drop edits here today and I’ll finalize by EOD.

(reaction :thumbsup: x3)

Nadia Rahman: one more nuance for mismatch: cached tokens can show as “cached” but still have non-zero cost depending on pricing model (esp. dedicated). folks will interpret cached=0. maybe add: “Cached tokens may still incur compute depending on deployment/pricing.”

Rishi Malhotra: +1. keep it non-committal: “Cached token handling varies by deployment mode.”

Dev Patel: added to known issues + will add a short line in mismatch macro: “Cached tokens are broken out for transparency; how they impact cost can vary by deployment mode/pricing.”

Kevin Osei: and please include: “Exports are audit logged” macro snippet. I’ll send exact phrasing:
“Export creation and download are recorded in audit logs (who, when, filters, and report metadata) for compliance review.”

Dev Patel: done. thanks all.
